declaration.preface:
Eco Jute Pvt. Ltd. is committed to respecting and protecting labour rights and human rights across its operations and business relationships. We strive to provide a workplace that promotes fair working conditions, equal opportunity, employee development, open communication, and safe and healthy working environments.

The Company supports career growth and training, encourages social dialogue and employee engagement, and is committed to maintaining a workplace free from child labour, forced labour, human trafficking, discrimination, harassment, and any form of abuse or exploitation.

Eco Jute Pvt. Ltd. expects all employees, contractors, suppliers, and business partners to uphold these principles and comply with applicable labour laws and human rights requirements. Through responsible employment practices and continual improvement, we aim to foster a respectful, inclusive, and productive workplace for all.
declaration.declaration:
Labour and human rights considerations are integrated into our business operations, employment practices, and workplace management systems. We establish objectives and initiatives to promote employee well-being, fair working conditions, workplace safety, equal opportunity, employee development, and respect for human rights.

Eco Jute Pvt. Ltd. provides appropriate resources, responsibilities, training, and awareness programmes to support these commitments. Through employee engagement, open communication, grievance mechanisms, monitoring, and continual improvement, we strive to maintain a safe, inclusive, and respectful workplace for all.
declaration.scope:
This Policy applies to all employees, contractual workers, trainees, contractors, and other persons working on behalf of Eco Jute Pvt. Ltd. It also extends to suppliers, service providers, and business partners where relevant.

The Policy covers labour and human rights matters across the Company's operations, including health and safety, working conditions, social dialogue, career management and training, prevention of child labour, forced labour and human trafficking, and prevention of discrimination and harassment.

focusAreas: Protection from Child and Forced Labour

Responsible Recruitment & Employment: Promote transparent, fair, and non-discriminatory recruitment practices.
Ensure employees receive clear employment terms and understand their rights and responsibilities.
Prevent recruitment-related exploitation and unfair practices.
Workplace Health, Safety & Well-Being: Maintain a safe, healthy, and secure workplace.
Prevent workplace injuries, unsafe conditions, and occupational health risks.
Promote employee awareness of workplace health and safety responsibilities.
Fair Employment Practices: Promote fair wages, reasonable working hours, lawful overtime, and transparent employment conditions.
Prevent unjustified wage deductions and excessive working hours.
Employee Engagement & Social Dialogue: Respect employees’ rights to freedom of association and collective representation.
Promote open communication between employees and management.
Provide accessible grievance and feedback mechanisms.
Learning, Development & Career Growth: Promote continuous learning, employee development, and opportunities for career progression.
Build employee skills relevant to their roles and responsibilities.
Protection from Child and Forced Labour: Maintain zero tolerance for child labour, forced labour, bonded labour, compulsory labour, and human trafficking.
Ensure employment is voluntary and free from coercion.
Support appropriate remediation if a child labour case is identified.
Equality, Inclusion & Respectful Workpla: Maintain a workplace free from discrimination, harassment, bullying, and retaliation.
Promote equal opportunity and respectful treatment of all employees.
Encourage employees to report concerns without fear.
Employee Privacy & Personal Data Protect: Protect employee personal and confidential information from unauthorized access, use, disclosure, or loss.
Ensure employee information is handled responsibly and only for legitimate purposes.
Restrict access to employee records to authorized personnel only.

policy.monitoring:
Labour and human rights information relating to employee welfare, working conditions, health and safety, working hours, wages, training, grievances, and other relevant indicators shall be compiled and reviewed periodically.

Human Resources (HR) Manager in coordination with the Sustainability & Compliance Officer, shall provide periodic reports to Senior Management on labour and human rights performance, key risks, incidents, grievances, compliance status, and progress against established objectives and targets.

Labour and human rights incidents, complaints, discrimination, harassment, child labour, forced labour, unsafe working conditions, and other concerns shall be reported through established channels, investigated appropriately, and followed by corrective actions where required.

Findings from employee feedback, workplace assessments, audits, inspections, grievance reviews, and risk assessments shall be communicated to relevant functions to support continual improvement.

Eco Jute Pvt. Ltd. may communicate relevant labour and human rights information to customers, regulatory authorities, certification bodies, business partners, and other interested stakeholders, as appropriate.

Labour and human rights disclosures, customer submissions, certifications, and regulatory information shall be prepared in accordance with applicable legal, contractual, and stakeholder requirements.

Information intended for external communication shall be reviewed by the responsible function to ensure accuracy, consistency, confidentiality, and appropriate supporting records.

Eco Jute Pvt. Ltd. shall engage with employees, employee representatives, suppliers, contractors, customers, regulatory authorities, and other relevant stakeholders on labour and human rights matters where appropriate.

Employee and stakeholder feedback, concerns, expectations, and improvement suggestions shall be considered when reviewing labour and human rights objectives, targets, programmes, and workplace practices.

The Company shall promote open communication and constructive dialogue to support fair employment practices, employee well-being, respect for human rights, and continual improvement.
policy.reviewMechanism:
Labour and human rights objectives, targets, and key performance indicators relating to employee welfare, health and safety, working conditions, training, wages, grievances, and human rights shall be reviewed annually.

Progress against established targets, workplace performance, compliance status, significant concerns, and improvement initiatives shall be evaluated through periodic Management Review Meetings.

Key achievements, challenges, risks, and opportunities for improvement shall be identified and documented to support informed decision-making.

Findings from workplace assessments, audits, inspections, grievance reviews, risk assessments, incident investigations, employee feedback, and stakeholder engagement shall be used to identify opportunities for improvement.

Corrective and preventive actions shall be implemented where labour or human rights concerns, non-compliances, workplace incidents, or performance gaps are identified.

Labour and human rights objectives, targets, programmes, and workplace practices shall be reviewed and updated periodically to strengthen employee well-being and address emerging risks.

Human Resources (HR) Manager shall review this Policy at least once every two years, or earlier where significant changes occur in labour laws, business operations, workforce requirements, identified risks, or stakeholder expectations.

Any revisions to the Policy shall be reviewed and approved by Senior Management before implementation.

Approved changes shall be communicated to relevant employees, contractors, and other applicable stakeholders, with appropriate training and awareness provided where required.
